description: Add mild bilateral lower extremity trace edema on exam
presentation: A 50-year-old man with IgA nephropathy, diabetes insipidus, and recurrent UTIs presents with suspected drug allergy after Bactrim for UTI: pruritus and hives on arms/trunk began after the 4th dose; patient self-discontinued after the following dose. He also noted dark urine, and labs showed AKI (Cr 2.5 from baseline 1.2) that resolved over the next month. On exam, mild bilateral lower extremity trace edema was noted. He previously tolerated once-daily low-dose Bactrim for 6 months 10 years ago. Does the patient need sulfa allergy testing? Is the AKI was part of an allergic reaction or a separate adverse effect?
